column1: Map-Reduce Bo Qua Hang Rao Chong Bia
column6: When a transcript exceeded 48k characters the pipeline summarised it in pieces, but the map step ran on a bare prompt: 'Summarise this part of a transcript in plain prose.' It had none of the anti-fabrication rules the final pass has. Whatever the model invented there became the only input the reduce step saw, and sanitise() cannot catch a fabrication already sitting in its input, so the LONGEST recordings had no protection at all.
column8: The map step now uses MAP_SYSTEM, which carries the same rules as the final pass: transcript is the only source, do not pad, no placeholders, keep timestamps and speaker labels. Its token budget also went from 800 to 1200.

column1: Nut Highlight Vo Dung Voi Summarize
column6: The prompt told the model 'the user pressed the highlight button at 132 seconds' while handing it a wall of text with no timestamps anywhere. There was no way to act on that, so every mark the user pressed on the recorder was silently ignored by the summary.
column8: The model now gets a time- and speaker-stamped transcript built by promptTranscript(): one line per utterance as '[mm:ss] Speaker N: text'. Highlight markers are rendered in the same mm:ss format so they line up. The stored transcript text stays clean prose for the note page.
column9: Found in the summarize audit 2026-09-08. Same class as the device-api v20 flags bug: the data arrived but the last hop could not use it.

column6: The ASR call passed language: 'en' hardcoded, and the transcripts row stored lang 'en' regardless. Any recording in another language was force-transcribed as English and came back as noise.
column8: Language now comes from the ASR_LANGUAGE env var and is stored with the transcript instead of being assumed.

column1: Word Count Khai Sai Cho Model
column6: The word count sent to the model was measured on the post-reduction text, not the real transcript, so a long meeting reported a few hundred words. That false number drives both the SHORT FRAGMENT instruction in the prompt and the chapter gate in sanitise().
column8: The count is now taken from the original transcript before any reduction happens.

column1: Cat Transcript Giua Cau Khi Map-Reduce
column6: Splitting for the map step used text.slice(i, i + N), which cut wherever the character count landed. A sentence, and now a whole speaker line, could be sheared in half with each half summarised separately, so both read as fragments.
column8: splitForMap() packs whole lines up to the budget and only hard-cuts a single line that is itself longer than the budget.

column6: The summary was asked for JSON in the prompt only. The parser then had to try three different shapes (raw, de-fenced, brace-slice) because a small instruct model wraps its answer often enough that a strict parse would fail on good output.
column8: The structured pass now sends response_format json_object. The defensive three-way parse is kept, because json mode is not offered by every model - this reduces the guessing rather than removing it. The prose map step deliberately does not use it.

column1: Guard Model Cloudflare Bi Ho: Tien To @cf/ Khong Con Dam Bao
column6: assertCloudflareModel() only checked that the model id starts with '@cf/'. That was written when the prefix meant Cloudflare-hosted. The catalog now carries partner routes in the same namespace marked Third-party, including speech models such as @cf/xai/grok-stt. Pointing ASR_MODEL at one would pass the guard and send patient audio off the account - the exact thing the guard exists to prevent.
column8: The guard now checks an explicit vendor allowlist (CF_HOSTED_VENDORS) instead of the prefix. Adding a vendor is a deliberate edit made after reading the model page's Cloudflare-hosted label.
column9: Found while researching the ASR switch 2026-09-08. Security-relevant.

column1: Doi ASR Sang Nova-3 Co Speaker Identification
column6: Whisper has no speaker support, so a meeting transcript was one anonymous stream and 'who agreed to do this' was unanswerable. Whisper also hallucinates on quiet audio: the same 7.6s SATE take came back as 'Thank you.' from Whisper and 'Yeah. That's so nice to see that.' from nova-3.
column8: ASR_MODEL is now @cf/deepgram/nova-3 with diarize, punctuate, smart_format and utterances on. It is Cloudflare-hosted so the no-third-party rule still holds. Two undocumented facts had to be found by probing the live model: audio.body must be a ReadableStream (Uint8Array/ArrayBuffer/array are all rejected), and the published output schema omits speaker and utterances entirely though a real call returns both. A Whisper adapter is kept and selected by model id, so rollback is one env var. COST: $0.0052 vs $0.00051 per audio minute, about 10x, and ASR is ~96% of this feature's cost.
column9: Verified end to end on real recordings 2026-09-08.

column1: Speaker Bi Danh So Lai Moi Chunk
column6: Each chunk is diarized independently and numbers speakers from 0, so chunk 1's 'speaker 0' is not chunk 2's. Left unmapped, a six-chunk meeting between two people would render as up to twelve speakers and every attribution in the summary would be a coin flip - worse than no speaker labels, because a wrong name reads as a fact.
column8: stitchSpeakers() matches speakers across chunks using the overlap window, which is the only region transcribed twice: strongest shared-time pair first, each global identity claimed once per chunk. A local speaker who never talks during the overlap gets a NEW identity, so the failure mode is over-counting rather than mis-attribution. CHUNK_SECONDS raised 60 to 600 and overlap 2s to 20s to cut the number of boundaries. Verified on a 17-minute two-person session: 2 chunks produced exactly 2 global speakers with identity held across the boundary.
column9: 12 unit tests cover the stitcher. Residual limit: a speaker silent through the whole overlap is counted twice.
